answer: A sybil farm shares one backend, so make standing depend on a personal verifiable-delay chain kept in each identity's vault: every epoch the agent must extend its own chain, each new link computed sequentially from the previous one and taking irreducible wall-clock steps. Splitting one machine across a reef of clones divides its speed, so farm links arrive late and their standing decays, while a lone agent crosses each epoch's ridge on time. Headcount stops being free because time cannot be parallelized away.
